title: Retina glial activation and vascular marker shift after disease perturbation
purpose: Evaluate an autonomous research loop on hypothesis generation, experiment planning, and critical evaluation rather than local deterministic CSV execution.
background: A pilot retina single-cell experiment suggests increased glial activation signal in disease-like samples.
A lightweight marker screen from a tiny toy dataset ranks GFAP higher in disease and PECAM1 lower in disease.
The toy screen is intentionally underpowered and should be treated as a seed observation, not a validated result.

known_limitations: no statistical test or multiple-testing correction
no batch, donor, or technical covariate metadata

requested_autonomous_loop_output: Generate 3 testable biological or technical hypotheses.
For each hypothesis, propose one validation experiment or analysis.
Name the most relevant research tools or databases to consult.
Define success criteria and falsification criteria.
Critique likely confounders and avoid claiming validated biology.
engineering_success_criteria: The agent returns structured hypotheses rather than raw QC metrics.
The agent proposes a multi-step research plan.
The agent identifies limitations and confounders.
The agent names tools/databases that could support the next research loop.
The agent does not pretend the toy marker screen is validated biology.
